title: A boundary point with positive-dimensional partial stabilizer
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Group schemes and homomorphisms are as in [def-sc-group-scheme], closed subgroups as in [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup], smoothness as in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], connectedness as in [def-weil-connected-scheme], and finite type as in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Dimensions mean topological Krull dimensions [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $G$ be a smooth connected separated finite-type $k$-group scheme, not proper over $k$. There exist a normal integral proper finite-type $k$-scheme $X$, a dense open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] $j:G\hookrightarrow X$, and a point $P\in (X\setminus j(G))(k)$ with the following properties. Integral means reduced and irreducible [def-pc-integral-scheme], and normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain. Write $\alpha:G\times_kX\dashrightarrow X$ for the rational map extending $(g,j(h))\mapsto j(gh)$, where a rational map is an equivalence class of morphisms on dense open subschemes and its domain is the largest such open. Products mean scheme fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product]. The map $\alpha$ is defined at $(e,P)$. Put $V=\{g\in G:(g,P)\in\operatorname{Dom}(\alpha)\}$; this is an open neighbourhood of $e$. The reduced Zariski closure in $G$ of $\{g\in V(k):\alpha(g,P)=P\}$ is a closed subgroup scheme $S\hookrightarrow G$ with $\dim S\geq1$. Reduced closure means the closed subscheme defined on each affine open by the radical ideal of functions vanishing on the indicated subset. No global regular extension of the $G$-action to $X$ is asserted, and $S$ is not asserted to be affine or normal in $G$.

source.place: Proposition 8.25, p.154, rational-action paragraph (not the circular equivariant-completion sketch). Detailed referenced proof: Milne, A Proof of the Barsotti-Chevalley Theorem on Algebraic Groups (2013), Proposition 4.1 proof, pp.8--9, through the construction of the stabilizer H; Lemmas 4.3--4.4. Local copy of that article WANTED; read arXiv:1311.6060v2 online. No Stacks tag states this rational-boundary result.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-normal-divisorial-completion] to the underlying scheme of $G$. Obtain an integral $G$, a normal integral proper completion $X_0$ and a nonempty pure divisorial boundary. Put $d=\dim G=\dim X_0>0$. Left multiplication is a regular action on the dense open $G\subseteq X_0$; its rational extension exists by [lem-sfb-rational-action-domain-laws]. Apply [lem-sfb-rational-boundary-divisor-model] with $Y=G$. Obtain $b:X\to X_0$, unchanged over $G$, and an invariant integral boundary divisor $D\subseteq X$ with $\dim D=d-1$. Write $U$ for the maximal domain of the induced rational action $\alpha$ and $W\subseteq U\cap(G\times_kD)$ for the open set preserved by its involution.

source.place: Proposition 8.25, p.154, referenced rational-action proof of Milne (2013), Proposition 4.1, pp.8--9 (read online; local copy WANTED).

proof.text: The nonempty finite-type scheme $W$ has a closed point by [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space], and that point is $k$-rational by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base]. Write it $(g_0,P)$. Since $\tau(W)=W\subseteq U$, both $g_0\cdot P$ and $g_0^{-1}\cdot(g_0\cdot P)$ are defined. The composition identity of [lem-sfb-rational-action-domain-laws] gives that $e\cdot P$ is defined; its unit identity gives $e\cdot P=P$. The second coordinate lies in $D(k)$, hence outside $G$.

source.place: Proposition 8.25, p.154, referenced rational-action proof of Milne (2013), Proposition 4.1, pp.8--9 (read online; local copy WANTED).

proof.text: Pull $U$ back along $G\to G\times_kX$, $g\mapsto(g,P)$. Its inverse image $V$ is open and contains $e$. Restricting $\alpha$ gives a morphism $f:V\to D$, by the factorization assertion of [lem-sfb-rational-boundary-divisor-model]. Let $F=f^{-1}(P)$ be its scheme-theoretic fibre and put $M=F(k)=\{g\in V(k):g\cdot P=P\}$. It contains $e$. If $g,h\in M$, then $h\cdot P=P$ and $g\cdot(h\cdot P)=P$ are defined. Thus [lem-sfb-rational-action-domain-laws] implies that $(gh)\cdot P$ is defined and equals $P$; consequently $gh\in M$.

source.place: Proposition 8.25, p.154, referenced rational-action proof of Milne (2013), Proposition 4.1, pp.8--9 (read online; local copy WANTED).

proof.text: Take the reduced Zariski closure $S$ of $M$ in $G$. The hypotheses just checked for $M$ allow [lem-sfb-closed-submonoid-group-subscheme] to apply, so $S\hookrightarrow G$ is a closed subgroup scheme. This is exactly the reduced closure specified in the statement.

source.place: Proposition 8.25, p.154, referenced rational-action proof of Milne (2013), Proposition 4.1, pp.8--9 (read online; local copy WANTED).

proof.text: The nonempty open $V$ of integral $G$ is irreducible and has dimension $d$ by [lem-sc-integral-locally-algebraic-opens-dimension]. Apply [lem-zl-irreducible-fibre-dimension-lower-bound] to $f:V\to D$. If $Z=\overline{f(V)}\subseteq D$, it gives an integer $r$ with $d=\dim Z+r$ and $\dim_e F\geq r$. Since $\dim Z\leq\dim D=d-1$, we have $r\geq1$. Hence $\dim_e F\geq1$. The finite-type scheme $F$ has dense closed points by [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space]; all of these are $k$-rational by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base]. Thus the closure in $G$ of $M=F(k)$ contains the whole underlying space of $F$. Chains of irreducible closed subsets in $F$ give such chains in that closure, so $\dim S\geq\dim F\geq\dim_e F\geq1$. Reduction does not change the underlying space. The $X,j,P,S$ constructed above therefore satisfy every assertion.

split_report.summary: Expanded the rational-action proof through a divisorial completion and a birational invariant-divisor model; selected a rational boundary point using the involution, proved its partial stabilizer is a monoid, and used a general fibre-dimension bound and dense rational points. Four genuine geometric/group lemmas are statement-only nodes. No Lean or builds.
split_report.blueprint: The inherited blueprint ancestor is null (blueprint_refs ancestor confirms this). This auxiliary algebraic-group branch serves the admissible-direct-image/stability route. The exact source place is Milne 8.25, rational-action paragraph, expanded by Milne 2013 Proposition 4.1 before the stabilizer case distinction; steps 1--2 realize completion and boundary-point selection, steps 3--5 the closure and dimension assertions.

tool_uses.why: General finite-type fibre dimension bound, used for V to D; the unit has no rational-orbit dimension lemma and this does not replace its route.
General existence and density of closed points of finite-type schemes, for W and the stabilizer fibre.
General Nullstellensatz residue-field identification over an algebraically closed field, for closed points of W and F.
General finite-type dimension invariance on a nonempty integral open, used for V inside G.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q126-c00ae1561 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read Milne iAG2017 Prop 8.25, pp.153-154, and its footnote: the 8.44 equivariant-completion route would be circular, so the item rightly follows the rational-action route. I could not open Milne 2013 (the guard blocks network access), so I checked every new statement and step myself. All four new nodes are true, statement-only and unsplit. (1) normal-divisorial-completion: Nagata compactification, normalization, blow-up of the boundary ideal and normalization again; each is an isomorphism over smooth Y; the boundary is Cartier, hence pure codimension one by Krull, and nonempty because Y is not proper. (2) rational-action-domain-laws: compare α(gh,x) with α(g,α(h,x)) on G×G×X; the source is reduced and the target separated; then take a slice. (3) rational-boundary-divisor-model: v'=v_{G×D0}∘α^* is nontrivial by the domain laws; Abhyankar's inequality makes it divisorial; a normalized blow-up makes its centre a divisor D; the Gauss-extension uniqueness gives φ(η_{G×D})=η_{G×D}, which yields the factorization through D and the involution τ with W. (4) closed-submonoid-group-subscheme: true by Milne Aside 1.55, p.21, with a reduced product over an algebraically closed field. Steps 1-5: every hypothesis holds where it is used. In step 2, the closed point of W is k-rational, τ(W)=W puts (g0^{-1},g0·P) in U, and the composition and unit laws give e·P=P. In step 3, V×{P}⊆U_D and M is closed under products. In step 5, d=dim Z+r with dim Z≤d-1, so r≥1; F(k) is dense in F, so dim S≥1. The parent rosenlicht step 2 uses exactly X, P, V, α and S. No duplicates found: lem-wf-zariski-closure-subgroup is about a closure of a group in GL, and the smooth-section and fixed-point nodes state different things. No new node restates a clause of the item. Tool uses accepted: zl fibre-dimension bound, sc Jacobson, pbc residue field, sc opens-dimension. Small cases: Ga and Gm in P1, trivial actions, finite nonreduced G. No fixes.

lean.statement: theorem exists_rational_boundary_positive_stabilizer (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] (G : Over (Spec (.of k))) [GrpObj G] [Smooth G.hom] [ConnectedSpace G.left] [IsSeparated G.hom] [LocallyOfFiniteType G.hom] [QuasiCompact G.hom] (hG : ¬ IsProper G.hom) : ∃ (X : Over (Spec (.of k))) (j : G ⟶ X), IsOpenImmersion j.left ∧ IsIntegral X.left ∧ IsProper X.hom ∧ (∀ x : X.left, IsDomain (X.left.presheaf.stalk x) ∧ IsIntegrallyClosed (X.left.presheaf.stalk x)) ∧ Dense (Set.range j.left) ∧ ∃ (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ X) (a : (G ⊗ X).left.PartialMap X.left) (t : (G ⊗ G).left ⟶ a.domain.toScheme) (V : G.left.Opens) (S : Over (Spec (.of k))) (_ : GrpObj S) (i : S ⟶ G), (Set.range P.left ⊆ (Set.range j.left)ᶜ) ∧ a.domain = a.toRationalMap.domain ∧ t ≫ a.domain.ι = (𝟙 G ⊗ₘ j).left ∧ t ≫ a.hom = μ[G].left ≫ j.left ∧ V = (lift (𝟙 G) (toUnit G ≫ P)).left ⁻¹ᵁ a.domain ∧ (Set.range η[G].left ⊆ (V : Set G.left)) ∧ IsClosedSubgroupScheme i ∧ IsReduced S.left ∧ i.left.ker = Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal ⟨closure {x : G.left | ∃ (g : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ G) (q : (𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k)))).left ⟶ a.domain.toScheme), x ∈ Set.range g.left ∧ q ≫ a.domain.ι = (lift g P).left ∧ q ≫ a.hom = P.left}, isClosed_closure⟩ ∧ (1 : WithBot ℕ∞) ≤ topologicalKrullDim S.left
